correctness.rationale: For a general matrix with columns T(1)=(a,b) and T(epsilon)=(c,d), direct basis substitution into the averaging identity gives exactly bc=0, b(a-d)=0, cd=0, and d(a-d)=0. Solving these equations yields precisely two affine planes with intersection {0}. Every automorphism is diag(1,s), s nonzero, so conjugation rescales the single off-diagonal parameter on each plane and gives the four stated normal-form families. The finite-field counts follow by orbit-stabilizer counting and are independently replayed by exhaustive enumeration over F_2, F_3, F_5, and F_7.

value.rationale: The dual numbers are the canonical smallest nonsemisimple unital local algebra and encode first-order infinitesimal structure. The 2023 framework turns averaging operators into associative dialgebra structures, so a complete automorphism quotient on this base algebra supplies reusable normal forms rather than an arbitrary coefficient slice. The result also exposes a simple reducible geometry—two affine planes meeting at one point—and gives exact finite-field moduli counts in every characteristic.
